interface.signature: solve(t: int, test_cases: list[tuple[int, int, int, list[tuple[int, int, int]], list[tuple[int, int]]]]) -> list[str]

preconditions.description: The number of test cases is between 1 and 50 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= N <= 1000 for (N, P, M, _, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of students (computers) N is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(N - 1 <= P <= 100000 for (N, P, M, _, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of connections P is at least N-1 (minimum spanning tree edges) and at most 100000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= M <= 100000 for (N, P, M, _, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of queries M is between 1 and 100000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= N and 1 <= v <= N for (N, P, M, _, queries) in test_cases for (u, v) in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query in every test case, u and v are valid computer indices between 1 and N inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= d <= 1000000 for (N, P, M, connections, _) in test_cases for (u, v, d) in connections)
preconditions.description: For each connection in every test case, the distance d is between 1 and 1000000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set((u, v, d) for (u, v, d) in connections)) == len(connections) for (N, P, M, connections, _) in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Within each test case, all connections (u, v, d) are unique (no duplicate edges).

postconditions.expression: len(output) == t and all('Case: ' in line for line in output)
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one line per test case, each starting with 'Case: ' followed by the case number.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_lines) == M + 1 for output_lines in [line.split('\n') for line in output] if line.count('\n') > 0)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output contains exactly M+1 lines (case header + M query answers).

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= answer <= 1000000 for answer in [int(line) for line in output_lines[1:] if line.strip().isdigit()] for output_lines in [line.split('\n') for line in output] if line.count('\n') > 0)
postconditions.description: Each query answer is a valid positive integer distance (1 to 1000000).

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= u <= N and 1 <= v <= N for (N, P, M, _, queries) in test_cases for (u, v) in queries for i, output_lines in enumerate([line.split('\n') for line in output] if line.count('\n') > 0) for j, line in enumerate(output_lines[1:]) if i == (N, P, M, _, queries).index((N, P, M, _, queries)) and j == queries.index((u, v)) and line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) == min_distance_in_mst(u, v, connections))
postconditions.description: For each query (u, v), the answer is the minimum total distance between u and v in the minimum spanning tree (MST) of the given connections. The MST is constructed using all connections, and the distance is the sum of edge weights along the unique path between u and v in the MST.
